title: Cut and left-module prism are colour-equivalent operadic approximations
statement:
Use the operadic fibrations, category $L=N(\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes})$, pure-algebra subcategory $A$, inert arrows and sections of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $D=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, where $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$. Define $\mathrm{LCut}:D\to L$ by $[n]\mapsto(\langle n+1\rangle,\{n+1\})$. For $\beta=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[n]\to[m]$, with $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ monotone, its pointed map sends the indices $\alpha(j-1)<i\leq\alpha(j)$ to $j$ for $1\leq j\leq m$, sends $\alpha(m)<i\leq n+1$ to $m+1$, and sends $i\leq\alpha(0)$ to $*$. All non-basepoint fibres have their increasing order. Define $\mathrm{Cut}:D\to A$ by $[n]\mapsto(\langle n\rangle,\varnothing)$ and the same middle blocks, sending also all indices $i>\alpha(m)$ to $*$. The inert projection $\theta_n:\mathrm{LCut}([n])\to\mathrm{Cut}([n])$ discards index $n+1$ and fixes $1,\ldots,n$. These maps define the natural transformation $\gamma:D\times\Delta^1\to L$ from $\mathrm{LCut}$ to $\mathrm{Cut}$.

Both $\mathrm{Cut}:D\to A$ and $\gamma:D\times\Delta^1\to L$ are approximations in the sense of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. Each induces an equivalence on its colour fibre over $\langle1\rangle$: the former fibre is the single object $[1]$ and maps to $a$; the latter fibre has exactly the two discrete objects $([1],1)$ and $([0],0)$ and maps to $a$ and $m$, respectively. No claim that the displayed functors themselves are categorical fibrations is made; the approximation definition allows categorical-fibration replacement.

Their inert markings have the following explicit description. A top edge $([n],1)\to([m],1)$ is marked exactly when $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ is an interval inclusion, that is $\alpha(j)=\alpha(0)+j$ for every $j$. A bottom edge $([n],0)\to([m],0)$ is marked exactly when $\alpha$ is an interval inclusion with $\alpha(m)=n$. Every vertical edge $([n],0)\to([n],1)$ is marked. A cross edge $([n],0)\to([m],1)$ is marked exactly when $\alpha$ is an interval inclusion; it factors as the vertical edge at $[n]$ followed by that marked top edge. All these assertions concern the explicit ordinary operators and their nerves, independently of any target operadic fibration, algebra, module, or section category.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 4.1.2.9 and Proposition 4.1.2.11 (Cut approximation), Construction 4.2.2.6 and Remark 4.2.2.8 (the left-module prism is an approximation); Definition 2.3.3.6 specifies the approximation property. The inert marking is computed from the displayed blocks; compare Remark 4.2.2.26. Online source read; WANTED archive Higher Algebra in literature/. No Stacks tag covers this combinatorial infinity-operadic assertion.
